The Warden Lords manipulate this grim economy with cruel mastery:

Orchestrating rivalries, pushing hopeful adventurers to betray and kill each other, ensuring maximum death and despair.
Controlling information and “treasure maps,” feeding false hope and drawing more victims to the dungeon’s maw.
Branding the “chosen” survivors as saints or martyrs, exploiting their stories to recruit others while concealing the true cost.
Collecting relics from the fallen, using them to weave potent curses and dark blessings that tighten the Church’s grip on the world.

The dungeon itself is a manifestation of the Church’s corruption—cursed, endless, and hungry. The ancient wards and soul-bound traps imprison not just bodies, but the very essence of those who perish within, feeding the insatiable appetite of the Throne of Thorns.
The Church is a wolf in sheep’s clothing: a beacon of hope and salvation for the desperate, but in truth a devouring beast that grows stronger with every lost soul.
To enter the Leviathan’s Hoard is to accept a death sentence disguised as opportunity—a merciless gamble where the price of failure is not just flesh, but soul.

entries.name: Onigashima no Ōkoku
entries.content:
Onigashima no Ōkoku – The Demon Isle Kingdom
A Realm Beyond the Black Current’s Snare

Far to the east, beyond the reach of any known map, lies Onigashima—a cursed archipelago wreathed in eternal storm, where the sea itself rejects outsiders. To reach this forsaken land, one must sail through Kuroshio no Wana ("The Black Current’s Snare"), a two-year voyage through hellish waters where:
The fog drowns voices mid-sentence, leaving crews whispering in terror.
Storms rise without warning, their winds howling with the voices of drowned sailors.
Compasses spin wildly, as if the island itself repels the touch of man.
Those who survive speak of jagged cliffs rising like the teeth of a submerged beast, and shores littered with the salt-bleached skeletons of ships that came before.

The Oni Lords’ Dominion
Each peak of Onigashima is ruled by a different Oni warlord, their territories marked by skull cairns and ribcage gates.

Kurote no Ō – The King of Black Hands
His fingers are ten skeletal blades, each carved from a different ship’s mast.
His fortress is built from petrified sailors, their faces still locked in screams.
He collects the first breath of newborns, stealing it before they can cry.

Shiranui no Hime – The Princess of Phantom Fire
Her hair is living blue flame, whispering secrets in a dead language.
She dances atop waves during storms, luring ships onto rocks with an impossible song.
Her palace is a coral labyrinth, where the drowned wander, searching for their lost voices.

Honebukuro no Yasha – The Sack-Boned Demon
His body is a stitched mass of stolen bones, constantly cracking and reforming.
He keeps victims alive inside him, their faces pressing against his ribs like prisoners.
His laughter sounds like a landslide of breaking spines.

The Cursed Land Itself
Onigashima is not just an island it is a living nightmare.
The trees have veins, pulsing with black sap. Their roots digest the unworthy, leaving hollowed-out husks.
The rivers flow uphill, carrying the whispers of those who drowned in them.

The moon here is red, casting shadows that move on their own.
Those who stay too long begin to change their bones warping, their skin hardening like bark. Some say the island feeds on time itself, making years feel like days and days like eternities.

The Shadowed Village – Humans Under the Oni’s Gaze
Nestled in the jagged foothills of Onigashima’s demon peaks, where the mist never fully lifts, lies Kageyado ( "Shadow Lodging")—a village of humans who have learned to survive in the shadow of the Oni Lords.

A Fragile Existence
The people of Kageyado live in constant tension—neither fully enslaved nor truly free. They offer tribute to the Oni in exchange for survival:

Harvest of Flesh – Every full moon, the strongest villager is sent to the mountains as an offering. Some return changed.
The Blood Brew – A dark wine fermented with Oni saliva, drunk to stave off the island’s curses. Those who refuse it wither within weeks.
The Bone Pacts – Carved agreements etched into human ribs, ensuring the Oni do not slaughter them outright.
Yet, despite the terror, some humans do more than survive—they thrive.

The Half-Blood Children
Not all who lie with Oni die. Some bear Hannya-ko ("Half-Demon Children") offspring of human and Oni blood.

Signs of the Blood
Unnatural Strength – Even as infants, they can crush stones in their grip.
Crimson Markings – Their skin bears swirling red patterns that darken with rage.
Forbidden Hunger – They crave raw meat, sometimes even fresh blood.
The village treats them with both fear and reverence. Some believe they are cursed, others see them as protectors—the only ones who can stand against the Oni if they ever turn on Kageyado.

The Fate of the Hannya-ko
Taken by the Oni – Some are claimed by their demon parents, disappearing into the mountains.
Hidden Among Humans – Others are raised in secret, their true nature whispered about but never confirmed.
Driven Out – A few are exiled, forced to live as bandits or mercenaries in the wilds.

Life in Kageyado
The village is a place of silent defiance and superstition.
The Oni-Scarred – Elders with missing limbs or patches of hardened skin, proof of past encounters.
The Whispering Shrine – A forbidden altar where villagers leave offerings of teeth and hair, begging the Oni for mercy.
The Night Watch – Men and women who patrol with torches made from Oni bones, the only fire that keeps the demons at bay.
The villagers know they are living on borrowed time. One day, the Oni may grow tired of their games.
